\title{\bfseries The Admission Substrate:\\[0.4em]
\large Refusal, Algebra, and Receipts}
\author{Sean Chatman}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
This paper consolidates three papers from the Chatman Equation thesis
series -- foundations, admission algebra, and receipt cryptography -- into
a single, clean-room-rewritten paper. It states the five-object Chatman
equation and the Rice-quarantine argument that admission cannot be a
semantic decision (Chapter~\ref{sec:chatman-rice}); the full admission
algebra of denial words, obligations, taxonomy, and pipeline composition
(Chapter~\ref{ch:algebra}); the lifecycle typestate category
(Chapter~\ref{ch:lifecycle}); the manufacturing morphism and the Bounded
Receipted Chatman Equation (Chapter~\ref{ch:brce}); the receipt-chain
cryptography and Faithful Chain Theorem (Chapter~\ref{ch:crypto});
Conservation of Consequence and the validator pipeline
(Chapter~\ref{sec:conservation}); signed receipts, content addressing, and
interoperability (Chapter~\ref{ch:signed}); the git-backed audit ledger
(Chapter~\ref{ch:ledger}); and the Scope Theorem bounding what a verifying
receipt chain does and does not establish (Chapter~\ref{sec:scope}). Every
paragraph below is marked evidence-bound or speculative; every
machine-verification claim is reported per-lane (a bare-core Lean~4
kernel lane and a Mathlib lane) rather than as a single pass/fail, and
three reconciliation issues -- a disputed theorem, and two label
collisions -- are reported rather than resolved by fiat.
\end{abstract}
